title: Material culture
lead: Material culture is the first of the seven ideas, and it covers the physical side of a group’s way of life.

p: Material culture consists of physical objects associated with a group’s way of life. Objects can carry cultural meanings and help transmit traditions, while changing over time.
In plain words, material culture is the things you can see and touch that belong to a group’s way of life.

writers.name: Interactionists
writers.says: emphasise that an object’s significance is socially created: a flag is fabric, but people attach identity and meaning to it.

list: Traditional clothing at a cultural festival is a physical object that can express cultural identity.
A flag is material culture because it is fabric, but people attach identity and meaning to it.
Handmade decorations at a festival are physical objects that belong to a group’s way of life.
Festival food is also material culture, and sharing a family recipe with younger relatives may help to pass a tradition to another generation.
A school blazer with the school crest is a physical object that shows which school a pupil belongs to.
A smartphone is a physical object, and the way young people use it for group chats and photos is part of their everyday way of life.
